challenge.reason: The old decision is a security guardrail: secrets come from environment variables only and are never written under .faff/. The new decision writes resolved API keys in plaintext to .faff/cache/credentials.json, which directly breaches it. The argument does not hold up. Gitignored is not the same as not on disk: the file survives the session, gets picked up by backups, sandbox mounts, artifact uploads and tooling that copies .faff/, and goes stale after key rotation. The claimed benefit is negligible, since reading process.env is an in-memory lookup that costs far less than an LLM network call, and an in-process cache would get any saving without touching disk. No changed premise of the old decision is identified.
